content.value_statement: React UI work can miss loading states, validation, responsive layout, and accessibility details. This skill guides component reviews with concise React patterns and checklists.
actual_capabilities: Checks React components for loading, error, and empty states.
Recommends error boundary patterns for major UI sections.
Guides Zod and React Hook Form validation practices.
Highlights mobile-first CSS and touch target requirements.
Reviews accessibility basics, including semantic HTML, ARIA labels, keyboard support, and focus indicators.
limitations: Does not run tests, type checks, or lint commands by itself.
Does not replace a full accessibility audit with assistive technology.
Uses concise examples that may need adaptation for each codebase.
Does not cover backend logic or advanced state architecture.

use_cases.title: Review a New Component
use_cases.description: Find missing loading states, error states, helper placement issues, and navigation pitfalls before merge.

use_cases.title: Improve Form Behavior
use_cases.description: Check validation schemas, inline error display, and disabled submit states for React forms.

use_cases.title: Prepare Accessibility Checks
use_cases.description: Review semantic HTML, ARIA labels, keyboard behavior, focus indicators, and touch target sizing.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pitfalls-react skill to review this React component for loading states, error states, and helper placement: [paste component].

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pitfalls-react skill to check this form for Zod schema coverage, inline errors, and submit-state handling: [paste form].

prompt_templates.title: Audit Accessibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pitfalls-react skill to review this UI for semantic HTML, ARIA labels, keyboard support, and focus indicators: [paste code].

prompt_templates.title: Run Full React Pitfall Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pitfalls-react skill to audit this feature for component patterns, form validation, responsive behavior, error boundaries, and accessibility: [paste files].

output_examples.input: A React component renders data immediately and uses a clickable generic container.
output_examples.output: The review flags missing loading and error states, recommends semantic button behavior, and asks for keyboard support and focus styling.

output_examples.input: A form accepts values but shows validation only after submission.
output_examples.output: The review recommends schema validation, inline field errors, and a disabled submit state while validation or submission is active.

output_examples.input: A dashboard table works on desktop but overflows on small screens.
output_examples.output: The review suggests a mobile-first layout, horizontal table scrolling, and touch-friendly control sizes.

best_practices: Use the skill before merging React UI changes that add forms, navigation, or async data.
Provide complete component context, including loading, error, and empty-state behavior.
Pair the checklist with tests, linting, and manual accessibility checks.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the examples as a complete application architecture.
Do not skip browser and keyboard testing after applying the guidance.
Do not use generic containers for interactive controls when semantic elements are available.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews React components, forms, error boundaries, responsive layout, and accessibility basics.

faq.question: Does it execute project commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides written guidance and examples, but it does not run commands.

faq.question: Can it replace automated tests?
faq.answer: No. Use it with unit tests, integration tests, type checks, and linting.

faq.question: Is it useful for React Hook Form?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for React Hook Form, Zod schemas, inline errors, and submit states.

faq.question: Does it cover accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers semantic HTML, ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, focus indicators, and touch targets.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
